topic: Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors
question: What is the purpose of the outside left and right side convex mirrors on a school bus?
choice_a: To monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle, providing a view of traffic, clearances, and students at the side of the bus
choice_b: To provide a view directly behind the bus through a glass emergency door
choice_c: To see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus
choice_d: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
explanation: The manual states the convex mirrors are used to monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle, providing a view of traffic, clearances, and students at the side of the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

topic: Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors
question: When adjusting the outside convex mirrors on a school bus, what should you be able to see?
choice_a: Only the rear bumper and license plate area
choice_b: Only the area directly behind the bus for up to 400 feet
choice_c: The interior of the bus and all seated passengers
choice_d: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus
explanation: The manual instructs that convex mirrors should be positioned to see the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: Why must a school bus driver be careful when judging distance using the convex mirrors?
choice_a: Convex mirrors cannot be adjusted once installed
choice_b: Convex mirrors show a mirror image that is reversed left to right
choice_c: Convex mirrors only work at night
choice_d: Convex mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus
explanation: The manual specifically warns that convex mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their true size and distance from the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

topic: Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors
question: What is the primary purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors on a school bus?
choice_a: To see the front bumper 'danger zone' area directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision, plus the danger zone to the side of the bus
choice_b: To monitor students seated near the rear of the bus
choice_c: To give a wide-angle view of traffic approaching from behind
choice_d: To replace the need for the flat outside mirrors
explanation: Crossover mirrors, mounted on both front corners, are used to see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus and the danger zone areas to the side and near the service door and front wheel.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

topic: Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors
question: When properly adjusted, the crossover mirrors should allow the driver to see all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_a: The right and left front tires touching the ground
choice_b: The area from the front of the bus to the service door
choice_c: The rear bumper and everything within 400 feet behind the bus
choice_d: The entire area in front of the bus from the front bumper to the point where direct vision begins
explanation: Crossover mirrors are adjusted to show the front tires, the area to the service door, and the area in front of the bus to where direct vision takes over; the area behind the bus is monitored using the overhead inside mirror and side mirrors, not the crossover mirrors.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: How far behind a school bus can the blind spot area beginning at the rear bumper extend?
choice_a: Up to 100 feet or more
choice_b: Up to 400 feet or more
choice_c: Up to 200 feet or more
choice_d: Up to 1,000 feet or more
explanation: The manual states there is a large blind spot area that begins at the rear bumper and could extend up to 400 feet or more behind the bus, requiring use of exterior side mirrors to monitor that area.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: The overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus is used primarily to:
choice_a: Judge the danger zone directly in front of the bus
choice_b: Check tire condition before departure
choice_c: View traffic approaching from the sides
choice_d: Monitor passenger activity inside the bus
explanation: The manual states the overhead inside rearview mirror, mounted above the windshield, is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: Besides monitoring passengers, what may the overhead inside rearview mirror also provide limited visibility of?
choice_a: The undercarriage of the bus during inspection
choice_b: The engine compartment
choice_c: The area directly in back of the bus, if the bus has a glass-bottomed rear emergency door
choice_d: The fuel gauge and dashboard indicators
explanation: The manual notes this mirror may provide limited visibility directly in back of the bus if the bus is equipped with a glass-bottomed rear emergency door.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: About how far, or how many seconds, before a school bus stop should the alternating flashing amber warning lights be activated?
choice_a: Only after the bus has come to a complete stop
choice_b: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the stop
choice_c: At least 500 feet or approximately 20 seconds before the stop
choice_d: At least 50 feet or approximately 1-2 seconds before the stop
explanation: The manual states amber warning lights should be activated at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: About how far before pulling over should the right turn signal be activated when approaching a school bus stop?
choice_a: About 1,000 feet before pulling over
choice_b: Immediately upon seeing students at the stop, regardless of distance
choice_c: About 100-300 feet, or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over
choice_d: Only after the amber lights have been on for a full minute
explanation: The manual specifies turning on the right turn signal about 100-300 feet, or approximately 3-5 seconds, before pulling over for the stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: How far away from students at a designated stop should the front bumper of the school bus be when it comes to a full stop?
choice_a: At least 25 feet away
choice_b: At least 10 feet away
choice_c: Exactly at the curb, touching the stop location
choice_d: At least 50 feet away
explanation: The manual instructs bringing the school bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students, forcing them to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: After coming to a stop at a school bus stop, what should the driver do with the transmission and parking brake?
choice_a: Shut off the engine completely before opening the door
choice_b: Shift into reverse to hold the bus in place
choice_c: Leave the transmission in Drive and keep a foot on the service brake the entire time
choice_d: Place the transmission in Park, or in Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and set the parking brake at each stop
explanation: The manual requires placing the transmission in Park, or Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and setting the parking brake at each stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: Before opening the door and signaling students to approach, what final check should the driver make?
choice_a: Verify the fuel gauge reading
choice_b: Count the number of empty seats
choice_c: Confirm that all traffic has stopped
choice_d: Check the interior temperature
explanation: The manual states the driver should make a final check to see that all traffic has stopped before completely opening the door and signaling students to approach.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: According to the manual, how should students board the school bus?
choice_a: Two at a time, side by side
choice_b: Quickly, in any order, to save time
choice_c: Slowly, in single file, using the handrail
choice_d: Only after the driver has left the driver's seat
explanation: The manual instructs having students board the school bus slowly, in single file, and use the handrail.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: When loading students in the dark, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Turn off all interior lights to avoid blinding oncoming traffic
choice_b: Load students only at well-lit school campuses
choice_c: Use only the headlights for illumination
choice_d: Keep the dome light on while loading
explanation: The manual specifies that the dome light should be on while loading in the dark.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: Before moving the bus after loading, the driver should wait until:
choice_a: The dome light has been turned off
choice_b: The last student has paid the fare
choice_c: A parent signals from outside
choice_d: Students are seated and facing forward
explanation: The manual states the driver should wait until students are seated and facing forward before moving the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: If a school bus driver cannot account for a student who was near the bus during loading, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Assume the student went home and continue the route
choice_b: Proceed with the route and report it at the next stop
choice_c: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
choice_d: Radio the school and continue driving
explanation: The manual directs that if you cannot account for a student outside, you must secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: Which sequence correctly reflects the manual's steps for preparing to leave a stop after loading is complete?
choice_a: Release the parking brake, close the door, turn on left turn signal, engage transmission
choice_b: Turn on left turn signal, close the door, engage transmission, release parking brake
choice_c: Close the door, engage the transmission, release the parking brake, turn off alternating flashing red lights, turn on left turn signal, check all mirrors again, allow congested traffic to disperse
choice_d: Check mirrors, engage transmission, close door, release parking brake
explanation: The manual lists this exact order for preparing to leave: close the door, engage the transmission, release the parking brake, turn off the alternating flashing red lights, turn on the left turn signal, check mirrors again, and allow congested traffic to disperse.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: When loading students at the school campus, what additional step does the manual require before supervising loading?
choice_a: Activate the four-way flashers only
choice_b: Call the school office by radio
choice_c: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_d: Leave the engine running and open all windows
explanation: The manual states that when loading at the school campus, the driver should turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment before positioning to supervise loading.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: What must the driver do while unloading students on the route to confirm the location of all students before pulling away?
choice_a: Wait for a text message confirmation
choice_b: Rely on the parents waiting at the stop
choice_c: Count the number of students while unloading
choice_d: Ask a student assistant to sign a checklist
explanation: The manual instructs counting the number of students while unloading to confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: After exiting the bus during unloading on the route, how far should students walk away from the side of the bus?
choice_a: There is no specified distance
choice_b: At least 10 feet, to a position where the driver can plainly see all students
choice_c: Only 2 feet, just clear of the door
choice_d: At least 50 feet
explanation: The manual states students should exit and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all of them.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: If a school bus driver realizes they missed a student's unloading stop, what does the manual say to do?
choice_a: Turn around at the next intersection and return
choice_b: Call the student's parents and wait at the current location
choice_c: Do not back up; follow local procedures instead
choice_d: Immediately back up to the correct stop
explanation: The manual's note explicitly says if you have missed a student's unloading stop, do not back up, and to follow local procedures.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When a student must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, how far in front of the right corner of the bumper should the student walk, while remaining away from the front of the bus?
choice_a: Right up against the front bumper
choice_b: At least 30 feet in front of the bumper
choice_c: At least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper
choice_d: There is no specific distance given
explanation: The manual instructs the student to walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while remaining away from the front of the school bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: At the edge of the roadway, before crossing, what should a student check besides looking in all directions?
choice_a: Whether the driver has turned off the radio
choice_b: Whether other students have already boarded
choice_c: Whether the dome light is on
choice_d: Whether the red flashing lights on the bus are still flashing
explanation: The manual states that at the edge of the roadway, students should stop and look in all directions and check to see if the red flashing lights on the bus are still flashing before waiting for the driver's signal.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When crossing the roadway in front of the bus, where should a student stop a second time before continuing?
choice_a: At the left edge of the school bus, to look again for the driver's signal
choice_b: At the rear bumper of the bus
choice_c: In the middle of the roadway
choice_d: There is no second stop required
explanation: The manual instructs students to stop at the left edge of the school bus and look again for the driver's signal to continue crossing.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When unloading at the school, what should the driver do with the ignition switch and key before students exit?
choice_a: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_b: There is no requirement regarding the ignition at school
choice_c: Leave the engine running with the key in the ignition
choice_d: Leave the ignition on but remove the key
explanation: The manual states the bus should be secured at school by turning off the ignition switch and removing the key if leaving the driver's compartment.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

question: After students exit at school, what should the driver do to check for remaining students or items?
choice_a: Walk through the bus and check for hiding/sleeping students and items left by students
choice_b: Only check the front three rows
choice_c: Ask the last student to exit to check for others
choice_d: Assume the bus is empty once the door closes
explanation: The manual directs the driver to walk through the bus and check for hiding/sleeping students and items left by students after unloading at school.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

question: Before pulling away from the unloading area at school, what must the driver do in addition to fastening the safety belt and starting the engine?
choice_a: Wait exactly five minutes
choice_b: Turn on the dome light
choice_c: Sound the horn three times
choice_d: Engage the transmission, release the parking brake, turn off the alternating flashing red lights, turn on the left turn signal, and check all mirrors again
explanation: The manual's sequence for leaving the school unloading area includes engaging the transmission, releasing the parking brake, turning off the flashing red lights, turning on the left turn signal, and checking all mirrors again before allowing traffic to disperse.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: If a student drops an object near the bus during loading or unloading, what should the student be told to do?
choice_a: Leave the object and move to a point of safety, then try to get the driver's attention to retrieve it
choice_b: Wait at the location until the bus departs
choice_c: Ask another student to pick it up
choice_d: Immediately retrieve the object before boarding
explanation: The manual warns that stopping to pick up a dropped object can cause a student to disappear from the driver's sight at a dangerous moment, so students should leave the object, move to safety, and try to get the driver's attention.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.5 Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What is the danger described in the manual regarding 'Handrail Hang-ups'?
choice_a: Students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or body parts get caught in the handrail or door while exiting
choice_b: Handrails may detach if too many students use them at once
choice_c: Handrails obstruct the driver's view of the steps
choice_d: Handrails can become slippery in wet weather
explanation: The manual specifically warns that students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or even body parts get caught in the handrail or door as they exited the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.5 Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

question: What should a school bus driver do when a route or school activity trip is finished?
choice_a: Wait for the next driver to inspect the bus
choice_b: Only check the fuel level
choice_c: Immediately park the bus without further checks
choice_d: Conduct a post-trip inspection by walking through and around the bus
explanation: The manual requires a post-trip inspection, walking through the bus and around the bus, when a route or school activity trip is finished.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: During a post-trip inspection, which mirror-system-related items should receive special attention because they are unique to school buses?
choice_a: The radio antenna
choice_b: Only the rearview mirror
choice_c: The GPS navigation system
choice_d: Mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms
explanation: The manual lists mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms as items unique to school buses requiring special attention during post-trip inspection.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: As a general rule, how is student safety and control best maintained during an emergency or impending crisis?
choice_a: By immediately evacuating regardless of the situation
choice_b: By instructing students to call their parents
choice_c: By keeping students on the bus, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury
choice_d: By having students exit through the nearest window immediately
explanation: The manual states that as a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: If time permits, what should a school bus driver do before deciding to evacuate the bus?
choice_a: Consult the school bus manual for exact instructions
choice_b: Contact the dispatcher to explain the situation
choice_c: Ask the oldest student to make the decision
choice_d: Wait for the police to arrive
explanation: The manual instructs that if time permits, school bus drivers should contact their dispatcher to explain the situation before making a decision to evacuate.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: Under which of the following conditions MUST a school bus driver evacuate the bus?
choice_a: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_b: A student requests to be let off early
choice_c: The bus air conditioning has failed
choice_d: Whenever any mechanical warning light illuminates
explanation: The manual lists a bus stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing as one of the mandatory evacuation conditions, along with fire, imminent collision, hazardous position changes, and hazmat spills.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies (Mandatory Evacuations)

question: Which of the following is listed as a mandatory reason to evacuate a school bus?
choice_a: The bus is on fire or there is a threat of fire
choice_b: A tire is slightly underinflated
choice_c: The bus is more than 10 minutes behind schedule
choice_d: The heater is not working properly
explanation: The manual lists the bus being on fire or under threat of fire as a mandatory evacuation condition.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies (Mandatory Evacuations)

question: According to the manual, how far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic, should a 'safe place' generally be during an evacuation?
choice_a: At least 500 feet off the road
choice_b: At least 25 feet off the road
choice_c: Exactly at the roadside shoulder
choice_d: At least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic
explanation: The manual states a safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If fire is present during an evacuation, in which direction should the driver lead students?
choice_a: Downwind of the bus
choice_b: Directly toward the fire to assess it
choice_c: Back onto the bus for safety
choice_d: Upwind of the bus
explanation: The manual instructs leading students upwind of the bus if fire is present, so smoke and flames are less likely to reach them.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials, how far upwind should students be led?
choice_a: At least 10 feet
choice_b: There is no specific distance given
choice_c: At least 50 feet
choice_d: At least 300 feet
explanation: The manual states students should be led upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: During an evacuation near railroad tracks, in which direction should students be led?
choice_a: Toward the train to flag it down
choice_b: As far away from the tracks as possible and in the direction of any oncoming train
choice_c: Parallel to the tracks in either direction
choice_d: Onto the tracks to cross to the other side
explanation: The manual instructs leading students as far away from railroad tracks as possible and in the direction of any oncoming train.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If a school bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado and no building shelter is available, what should the driver direct students to do?
choice_a: Stand next to the bus for shelter
choice_b: Escort them to a nearby ditch or culvert, lying face down with hands covering their heads
choice_c: Stay seated on the bus with seatbelts fastened
choice_d: Run in different directions to spread out
explanation: The manual directs escorting students to a nearby ditch or culvert if shelter in a building is not available, having them lie face down with hands covering their heads, far enough away that the bus cannot topple on them.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: Which of the following is part of securing the bus before ordering an evacuation?
choice_a: Locking all doors from the outside
choice_b: Leaving the engine running for climate control
choice_c: Disconnecting the battery
choice_d: Placing the transmission in Park (or Neutral if no Park shift point), setting parking brakes, shutting off the engine, removing the ignition key, and activating hazard-warning lights
explanation: The manual lists securing the bus as placing the transmission in Park or Neutral, setting parking brakes, shutting off the engine, removing the ignition key, and activating hazard-warning lights.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If the radio is inoperable during an emergency, what is the manual's recommended order for getting help?
choice_a: Drive the disabled bus to the nearest phone
choice_b: Dispatch a passing motorist or area resident to call for help; as a last resort, dispatch two older, responsible students
choice_c: Immediately send all students to find help
choice_d: Wait at the scene until someone happens to stop
explanation: The manual says if there is no radio or the radio is inoperable, dispatch a passing motorist or area resident to call for help, and as a last resort, dispatch two older, responsible students to go for help.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: What does the manual say about moving a student believed to have a neck or spinal injury during an evacuation?
choice_a: Do not move the student unless his or her life is in immediate danger
choice_b: Only a paramedic may touch the student, so leave them exactly as found regardless of danger
choice_c: Move the student only if requested by the student
choice_d: Move the student immediately to the nearest safe place
explanation: The manual states not to move a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger, and that special procedures must be used if movement is necessary.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: After all students have evacuated, what should the driver do before joining the waiting students?
choice_a: Immediately drive the bus to the nearest repair shop
choice_b: Wait inside the bus for emergency responders
choice_c: Lock the bus and leave the scene
choice_d: Walk through the bus to ensure no students remain and retrieve emergency equipment
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to walk through the bus to ensure no students remain and to retrieve emergency equipment before joining the waiting students.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: What defines a 'passive' railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It has flashing red lights and gates
choice_b: It does not have any type of traffic control device, and the decision to proceed rests entirely with the driver
choice_c: It is only used by freight trains
choice_d: It is permanently closed to traffic
explanation: The manual defines a passive crossing as one without any traffic control device, requiring the driver to recognize the crossing, search for trains, and decide if it is safe to cross.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: What distinguishes an 'active' railroad-highway crossing from a passive one?
choice_a: Active crossings are marked only with pavement markings
choice_b: Active crossings do not require a stop under any circumstances
choice_c: Active crossings have a traffic control device such as flashing red lights, with or without bells and gates
choice_d: Active crossings are only found in rural areas
explanation: The manual describes active crossings as having a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, including flashing red lights with or without bells and gates.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

topic: Railroad Crossing Warning Signs and Devices
question: What does the round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign placed ahead of a railroad crossing tell the driver to do?
choice_a: Sound the horn continuously
choice_b: Change lanes to avoid the crossing
choice_c: Speed up to clear the crossing quickly
choice_d: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming
explanation: The manual states the advance warning sign tells the driver to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

topic: Railroad Crossing Warning Signs and Devices
question: What does the cross-buck sign at a railroad crossing require the driver to do?
choice_a: Stop only if a train is visibly approaching
choice_b: Yield the right-of-way to the train
choice_c: Use it only as a distance marker
choice_d: Proceed without stopping if no lights are flashing
explanation: The manual states the cross-buck sign marks the crossing and requires the driver to yield the right-of-way to the train.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

topic: Railroad Crossing Warning Signs and Devices
question: When the flashing red lights at a highway-rail grade crossing begin to flash, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Honk the horn and proceed cautiously
choice_b: Speed up to clear the crossing before the train arrives
choice_c: Wait exactly 30 seconds, then proceed regardless of the lights
choice_d: Stop, because a train is approaching and the driver must yield the right-of-way
explanation: The manual states that when the lights begin to flash, the driver must stop because a train is approaching, and the driver is required to yield the right-of-way to the train.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

topic: Railroad Crossing Warning Signs and Devices
question: At a gated railroad crossing, what should the driver do if the gate stays down after the train has passed?
choice_a: Wait exactly two minutes, then drive through
choice_b: Do not drive around the gate; instead, call the dispatcher
choice_c: Break through the gate with the vehicle
choice_d: Drive around the gate immediately
explanation: The manual instructs that if the gate stays down after the train passes, the driver should not drive around the gate but should instead call the dispatcher.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: How far before a railroad crossing should a driver activate hazard lights to make their intentions known?
choice_a: Approximately 200 feet before the crossing
choice_b: There is no recommended distance
choice_c: Approximately 1,000 feet before the crossing
choice_d: Only after coming to a stop at the crossing
explanation: The manual recommends activating hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing to make your intentions known.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At a railroad crossing, how close and how far should a school bus stop from the nearest rail?
choice_a: Exactly at the cross-buck sign, regardless of distance to the rail
choice_b: No closer than 50 feet and no farther than 100 feet
choice_c: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: As close as possible to see under the rail cars
explanation: The manual specifies stopping no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where the driver has the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: While stopped at a railroad crossing, what should the driver do with radios and passengers?
choice_a: Play an announcement over the PA system
choice_b: Turn the radio up to alert passengers
choice_c: Turn off all radios and noisy equipment and silence the passengers
choice_d: Allow passengers to talk freely as normal
explanation: The manual instructs turning off all radios and noisy equipment and silencing passengers at the crossing so the driver can listen for an approaching train.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At a multiple-track crossing, where should the driver stop before proceeding?
choice_a: There is no specific guidance for multiple tracks
choice_b: Only before the first set of tracks; when sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all tracks until completely clear
choice_c: Between each set of tracks, checking after every crossing
choice_d: Only after the last set of tracks
explanation: The manual states at a multiple-track crossing, stop only before the first set of tracks, and when sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all tracks until completely cleared.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: How should a school bus cross railroad tracks in terms of gear usage?
choice_a: Cross the tracks in a low gear and do not change gears while crossing
choice_b: Shift to neutral to coast across
choice_c: Accelerate hard and upshift while crossing
choice_d: Gear usage does not matter while crossing tracks
explanation: The manual instructs crossing the tracks in a low gear and not changing gears while crossing, since changing gears mid-crossing could cause a stall on the tracks.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: If a railroad crossing gate begins to come down after a school bus has already started crossing, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Drive through the gate even if it means breaking it
choice_b: Turn off the engine and evacuate immediately
choice_c: Stop immediately on the tracks and wait
choice_d: Reverse back off the tracks
explanation: The manual states that if the gate comes down after you have started across, drive through it even if it means you will break the gate, since stopping on the tracks is far more dangerous.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: If a school bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Try repeatedly to restart the engine before evacuating
choice_b: Get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving away from the tracks at an angle toward the train
choice_c: Wait inside the bus for a tow truck
choice_d: Push the bus off the tracks manually before evacuating
explanation: The manual instructs getting everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving everyone at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the direction of the train.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: According to the manual's 'containment or storage area' guidance, roughly how much extra length beyond the bus's own length should be added to determine an acceptable containment area on the far side of a crossing?
choice_a: Add 5 feet to the length of the school bus
choice_b: Add 50 feet to the length of the school bus
choice_c: No additional length is needed
choice_d: Add 15 feet to the length of the school bus
explanation: The manual states that as a general rule, you should add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: What should a driver do if there is no police officer at a railroad crossing and the driver believes the signal is malfunctioning?
choice_a: Call the dispatcher to report the situation and ask for instructions
choice_b: Proceed as normal, since the signal cannot be trusted anyway
choice_c: Disable the malfunctioning signal manually
choice_d: Wait indefinitely until someone else arrives
explanation: The manual instructs calling the dispatcher to report the situation and ask for instructions on how to proceed if the driver believes a signal is malfunctioning and no police officer is present.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: Why does the manual advise extra caution at 'passive' crossings even when active signals nearby indicate the tracks are clear?
choice_a: Because passive crossings have no traffic control device, so the driver must still look and listen to be sure it is safe to proceed
choice_b: Because passive crossings only occur at night
choice_c: Because passive crossings are always closer to schools
choice_d: Because passive crossings have faster trains
explanation: The manual warns to be especially careful at passive crossings, since even with active signals nearby indicating clear tracks, the driver must still look and listen to confirm it is safe.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: According to the manual, why shouldn't a driver deal with on-bus behavior problems while loading and unloading students?
choice_a: Loading and unloading requires all of the driver's concentration on what is happening outside the bus
choice_b: The dome light must remain off during any conversation
choice_c: Behavior problems only occur while the bus is moving
choice_d: It is against school policy to speak to students during loading
explanation: The manual states that loading and unloading requires all of the driver's concentration, and the driver should not take their eyes off what is happening outside the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.5.1 Don't Deal with On-bus Problems When Loading and Unloading

question: When handling a serious student behavior problem, how does the manual say the driver should speak to the offender?
choice_a: Yell to get the student's attention
choice_b: Immediately put the student off the bus at the nearest location
choice_c: Ignore the student entirely until reaching the school
choice_d: Stand up and speak respectfully, in a courteous manner with a firm voice, without showing anger
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to stand up and speak respectfully to the offender in a courteous but firm voice, reminding them of expected behavior without showing anger.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: Where is a driver permitted to put a student off the bus for a behavior problem?
choice_a: At the nearest police station
choice_b: At any convenient location along the route
choice_c: Only at school or at the student's designated school bus stop
choice_d: Wherever the other students agree is fair
explanation: The manual states a driver should never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: The Department of Transportation requires antilock braking systems (ABS) on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after which date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: January 1, 1995
choice_c: January 1, 2010
choice_d: March 1, 2005
explanation: The manual states the DOT requires ABS on air brake vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after which date must have ABS?
choice_a: March 1, 1995
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: January 1, 2000
explanation: The manual specifies hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999 must have ABS.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What is the main benefit of ABS when braking hard on a slippery surface?
choice_a: It automatically applies the parking brake
choice_b: It allows the driver to follow more closely at high speed
choice_c: It helps avoid wheel lock-up and maintain steering control, potentially allowing the driver to steer around an obstacle
choice_d: It significantly shortens stopping distance in every situation
explanation: The manual explains ABS helps avoid wheel lock-up and maintain control, so the driver may be able to steer around an obstacle while braking and avoid skids caused by over braking.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.2 How ABS Helps You

question: When braking hard in an emergency on a bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Release the brake completely and coast to a stop
choice_b: Apply the parking brake instead of the service brake
choice_c: Brake as usual, using only the force necessary to stop safely, and do not pump the brakes
choice_d: Pump the brakes rapidly
explanation: The manual states you should brake the same way regardless of ABS, using only the braking force necessary to stay in control, and that you should not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS in emergency braking.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

topic: Braking if ABS is Not Working
question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check, what does this indicate, and how should the driver respond?
choice_a: The tires need to be replaced immediately
choice_b: The vehicle has no brakes at all and must not be driven
choice_c: The engine has stalled and needs to be restarted
choice_d: ABS control may have been lost at one or more wheels, but the driver still has regular brakes and should drive normally while getting the system serviced soon
explanation: The manual explains that if the lamp stays on, ABS control may be lost at one or more wheels, but the driver still has regular brakes and should drive normally while getting the system serviced soon.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.4 Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: Which statement about ABS is TRUE according to the manual's safety reminders?
choice_a: ABS should help maintain vehicle control, but will not necessarily shorten stopping distance
choice_b: ABS increases the ultimate stopping power of the brakes
choice_c: ABS will necessarily shorten stopping distance in every case
choice_d: ABS allows you to drive faster and follow more closely
explanation: The manual states ABS won't necessarily shorten stopping distance; it will help maintain vehicle control but not always shorten stopping distance.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: According to the manual, ABS will NOT prevent which type of skid?
choice_a: Skids that occur only on wet pavement
choice_b: Skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_c: Any skid under any circumstance
choice_d: Skids caused by locking the front wheels while braking on ice
explanation: The manual clarifies that ABS should prevent brake-induced skids but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn (power or turning skids).
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: Is ABS a replacement for a vehicle's normal brakes?
choice_a: Yes, but only on vehicles built after 2005
choice_b: Yes, ABS replaces the need for normal brakes entirely
choice_c: No, ABS only functions when the parking brake is engaged
choice_d: No, ABS is an 'add-on' to normal brakes and does not increase or decrease ultimate stopping power
explanation: The manual states ABS won't increase or decrease ultimate stopping power because it is an 'add-on' to your normal brakes, not a replacement for them.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: When should the roof-mounted white strobe light on an equipped school bus be used?
choice_a: When you have limited visibility, meaning you cannot easily see around you in front, behind, or beside the bus
choice_b: At all times while the bus is in motion
choice_c: Only when requested by a passenger
choice_d: Only during loading and unloading of students
explanation: The manual states the overhead strobe light should be used when the driver has limited visibility, meaning it is difficult to see around the bus in front, behind, or beside it.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.7.1 Strobe Lights

question: Why do strong winds particularly affect the handling of a school bus?
choice_a: School buses have no traction control system
choice_b: The side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat, so strong winds can push it sideways or even tip it over
choice_c: Strong winds primarily affect the brakes, not the steering
choice_d: School buses are unusually light for their size
explanation: The manual compares the side of a school bus to a sail on a sailboat, explaining that strong winds can push the bus sideways, off the road, or even tip it over in extreme conditions.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.7.2 Driving in High Winds

question: What does the manual say about backing a school bus when students are outside of it?
choice_a: It is allowed if a lookout is posted
choice_b: It is only prohibited at school campuses
choice_c: You should never back a school bus when students are outside of the bus
choice_d: It is acceptable if done slowly
explanation: The manual states you should never back a school bus when students are outside of the bus, since backing is dangerous and increases the risk of a collision.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.7.3 Backing

question: What is the purpose of posting a lookout when backing a school bus?
choice_a: To give the driver turn-by-turn steering directions
choice_b: To operate the stop arm from outside the bus
choice_c: To count the students remaining on board
choice_d: To warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, without giving directions on how to back
explanation: The manual states the lookout's purpose is to warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, and that the lookout should not give directions on how to back the bus.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.7.3 Backing

question: If no lookout is available before backing a school bus, what should the driver do first?
choice_a: Wait for a student volunteer to check behind the bus
choice_b: Honk the horn and back up immediately
choice_c: Set the parking brake, turn off the motor, take the keys, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear
choice_d: Back up slowly without any additional checks
explanation: The manual instructs that with no lookout available, the driver should set the parking brake, turn off the motor, take the keys, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.7.3 Backing

question: If a driver must back up at a student pick-up point, what must be done regarding the students?
choice_a: Pick up students before backing, and watch for late comers at all times
choice_b: Have students board only after backing is complete
choice_c: Backing is never permitted at pick-up points under any circumstance
choice_d: Ask students to walk behind the bus to guide it
explanation: The manual states that if you must back up at a student pick-up point, be sure to pick up students before backing and watch for late comers at all times.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.7.3 Backing

question: How much tail swing can a school bus have, and what must the driver do to account for it?
choice_a: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, so the driver must check mirrors before and during any turning movement
choice_b: A school bus has no tail swing because of its long wheelbase
choice_c: Tail swing only matters when the bus is in reverse
choice_d: Tail swing on a school bus can exceed ten feet, requiring a spotter for every turn
explanation: The manual states a school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, and the driver needs to check mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor it.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 10, School Bus, 10.7.4 Tail Swing
